# Heat equation in three dimensions {#sec-heat3d}

`apps/heat3d` — the reference application for comparing discretisations,
because it ships several of them for the *same* PDE.

## Physical setting

Linear diffusion. The physics is not the point: this application exists so that
finite-difference order, spectral treatment, timing, and scaling can be
compared without the comparison being confounded by a difference in the
problem.

## Governing equations

$$
\partial_t u \;=\; D\,\nabla^2 u
$$ {#eq-h3-pde}

on a periodic box, with a single fixed $D$ shared by every binary so their
errors against the analytic solution are directly comparable.

For a single Fourier mode the exact solution is

$$
u_{\mathbf{k}}(t) \;=\; u_{\mathbf{k}}(0)\,e^{-D|\mathbf{k}|^2 t},
$$ {#eq-h3-exact}

which every driver is measured against.

## Finite-difference formulation

Centred stencils of even order $2m$ approximate the Laplacian,

$$
\partial_{xx}u\big|_i \;\approx\; \frac{1}{\Delta x^2}\sum_{j=-m}^{m} a_j\,u_{i+j},
$$ {#eq-h3-stencil}

with $m$ ghost cells exchanged per face before each evaluation. Orders 2
through 20 are available. Time stepping is explicit, subject to @eq-cfl.

## Spectral formulation

The spectral drivers use the same reciprocal-space convention as the rest of
the report. With $u = k_{\mathrm{lap}}$ the operator is simply $L(k) = D\,u$,
and the implicit Euler driver applies

$$
\hat u^{\,n+1} \;=\; \frac{\hat u^{\,n}}{1 - \Delta t\,D\,u},
$$ {#eq-h3-implicit}

which is two transforms per step and unconditionally stable.

## The five drivers

| Binary | Discretisation | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `heat3d_fd_scratch` | hand-written stencil | teaching: no framework abstractions |
| `heat3d_fd_manual` | fixed second order | manual halo management |
| `heat3d_fd` | orders 2–20 | convergence and order studies |
| `heat3d_spectral` | pointwise RHS | spectral evaluation of the RHS |
| `heat3d_spectral_pointwise` | implicit Euler, @eq-h3-implicit | unconditionally stable reference |

GPU twins `heat3d_fd_hip` and `heat3d_spectral_hip` mirror the FD and spectral
paths on device. **These two are what make @sec-scalability a method
comparison rather than an application comparison** — same equation, same
grids, same machine, two discretisations.

## Solution strategy

Explicit stepping for the FD drivers under @eq-cfl; implicit Euler in Fourier
space for the spectral drivers, at two transforms per step.

The trade is the usual one. The FD step is cheap and local — a stencil plus a
halo exchange with nearest neighbours — but the stable timestep shrinks as
$\Delta x^2$. The spectral step is unconditionally stable but costs two
all-to-all transforms, which is global communication. Which wins depends on the
accuracy required and on how well the machine's network carries an FFT
transpose; @sec-scalability measures exactly that.

## Verification

* **Analytic $L^2$ error.** Every driver is compared against @eq-h3-exact.
* **Observed order.** Measured convergence matches the design order of the
  stencil.
* **CPU/GPU agreement.** `HEAT3D_HIP_CHECKSUM` agrees between 1 and 16 GCDs to
  about $5\times10^{-15}$ relative; the spectral twin agrees to about
  $3\times10^{-16}$.

## Scalability

Measured on LUMI-G for both HIP twins, 1–32 GCDs. See @sec-scalability.
